analysis: Mostly docs plus a few Swift changes. Findings: (1) the new verified-weights cache (VerifiedWeightHashStore, DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE, configuration.md:371) lets the operator-owned stat-keyed record stand in for hashing at registration (T-012/T-027/A-004). Its integrity binding and the implementation were not in the supplied evidence. Also, GLM5NextManagedLoad publishes the catalog-pinned manifest aggregate as verifiedArtifactSHA256 on the assumption that the native loader SHA-256-verifies every core file; unverified here, and the load-time re-verification before serving needs checking in code. (2) SystemMemory reclaimable policy can over-admit loads (availability only). Examined and no regression found: GLM5NextWiredLimit and Notice are advice-only with no command execution, no prompt logging and fixed strings; EngineV2Bridge nativeOutputControlRefusal runs before any reservation, is content-free and returns a 400 so it avoids breaker strikes (T-010); the GLM withholding path for JSON and forced tools is fail-closed and releases the reservation; UsageSignal rename stores timing only; MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError maps the new typed error to 400. Not verifiable: the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (7bed821 to baca4ac), the truncated scheduler hunks, the variable-frame-rate video bounds (T-050), the callers of the renamed usage signal, and the FlintResponseFormat change. T-041 SSD cache posture is untouched. Integration source replay was incomplete (361 omitted units).

findings.detail: The new `DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE` (`~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json`) lets startup registration reuse a recorded weight hash instead of re-hashing when the stored device/inode/size/mtime/ctime match. The documented protection is only 'owner-only'. The owner is the provider operator (ADV-001), so the operator can hand-write a record for substituted weights, or edit the weights and restore their stat metadata. The provider would then register the previously verified hash without re-reading the bytes. This narrows the existing weight-substitution control (T-012/T-027) and adds an operator-writable trust input. The threat model should record that this cache is self-attested local state, not an integrity proof. If it is meant as a security control, MAC-bind it to the SE-rooted KEK or limit it to non-security fast paths. Implementation was not supplied, so this is an unverified contract.
findings.title: Weight-hash verification cache keyed on stat metadata with no stated integrity protection

findings.detail: On the default `reclaimable` policy, `availableBytes` now returns max(free+inactive, free-speculative+external_page_count+purgeable_count) (SystemMemory.swift lines 60-62, 83-86). `external_page_count` covers all file-backed pages, including actively mapped pages still in use and dirty pages needing writeback, so reclaiming them can cost refaults or writeback. The value feeds `ModelLoadAdmission.freeForLoadGb`/`maxLoadableWeightGb`. Heavy file-cache or mapped-file use on a shared host can therefore inflate headroom, so the provider admits a load or KV growth that causes swap or OOM pressure and degrades availability, and over-advertises capacity. Mitigation: credit only clean inactive file pages or a conservative fraction, or keep the stricter policy on shared hosts. `free-only` remains available.
findings.title: Default reclaimable policy credits all file-backed and purgeable pages as available memory, loosening load/KV admission
